frozen_candidate_root_contribution: In the Quran the root ح-ن-ف surfaces only as the single lexicalized adjective ḥanīf (sg. حَنِيفًا) and its plural (حُنَفَاءَ), always a state-descriptor (ḥāl or kāna-predicate), never a verb, maṣdar, or other derivative. Its narrowest defensible sense is: the standing state of exclusive, non-associating devotion oriented to Allah alone — set against shirk and against confessional (Jewish/Christian) identity. This is a manner of orientation, distinct from and additional to submission (muslim), devotion (qānit), sincerity (mukhliṣ), and good-doing (muḥsin), all of which are named separately beside it.

internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Every one of the 12 occurrences is the same one adjective describing a person or community as exclusively turned to Allah alone, not associating anything with Him and not belonging to a named confession. It is a quality/posture, not an act, and it is always accompanied by an explicit exclusion of shirk or a statement of exclusive devotion. Because the whole root is a single frozen adjective locked in a near-identical formulaic environment, the account fits all uses cleanly but cannot be graded as an established root-wide semantics.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Hnf does NOT entail: (1) a confessional/communal identity — explicitly not yahūdī and not naṣrānī (3:67), rejected as a communal label (2:135); (2) synonymy with islām/submission — 3:67 stacks 'ḥanīfan musliman' as two distinct qualifiers; (3) an action or event — the root never verbalizes, no maṣdar/participle beyond this adjective; (4) generic piety — it carries specific anti-associating content that qānit/muḥsin/mukhliṣ do not; (5) any 'inclining/turning-away' motion sense — that etymology is NOT Quran-internally demonstrable; the turning imagery is carried by wajjaha / aqim wajhaka (wjh, qwm), not by ḥanīf itself.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 3:67 (word_ref 3:67:9:1): 'mā kāna Ibrāhīmu yahūdiyyan wa-lā naṣrāniyyan wa-lākin kāna ḥanīfan musliman' — here ḥanīf sits inside a confessional taxonomy (yahūdī / naṣrānī / ḥanīf) and is paired with muslim (ḥanīfan musliman), pulling it toward a lexicalized Abrahamic identity label; the non-redundancy of the pairing still shows it contributes distinct anti-shirk exclusivity rather than 'submitter'. This is the occurrence that most resists a single compositional 'state-of-orientation' reading and most exposes how much the positive content is co-supplied by neighbouring terms.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: 'Lexicalized Abrahamic-identity epithet': ḥanīf is a frozen honorific of 'the milla of Ibrāhīm', its monotheist charge donated entirely by the recurring 'wa-mā kāna mina l-mushrikīn' negation rather than intrinsic. Support: 5/12 are the near-verbatim formula 'millata Ibrāhīma ḥanīfan' (16:123, 2:135, 3:95, 4:125, 6:161) and 8/12 are Ibrāhīm-bound. It is defeated as PRIMARY because the 4 non-Ibrāhīm uses (10:105, 30:30 commanded to the Prophet; 22:31, 98:5 of the plural community) carry the identical exclusive-devotion environment (ghayra mushrikīna bihi; mukhliṣīna lahu l-dīn) with no appeal to Abraham — the exclusivity content travels cleanly off the epithet. But because the term never appears outside the anti-shirk/Ibrāhīm frame, this competitor cannot be fully disproven, only shown less economical — the ceiling on confidence.

internal_discovery.rationale: All three lenses independently converge: (1) morphological monotony — the entire root is one faʿīl lexeme with sg/pl allomorphy only, so no root-vs-lexeme separation and no derivational spread to triangulate a nucleus; (2) all 12 sit in an anti-shirk / exclusive-devotion frame, and the sg/pl classes mutually reinforce (22:31 'ghayra mushrikīna bihi' and 98:5 'mukhliṣīna lahu l-dīn' gloss the singular's frame); (3) distinctiveness is genuine — 3:67's not-Jew/not-Christian contrast and the non-synonymy with muslim show ḥanīf does independent work, lifting it above WEAK; (4) STRONG is barred because a lexicalized nominal sub-class (the 'millata Ibrāhīma ḥanīfan' formula, 5/12) governs, apparent breadth is largely one repeated collocation, and the positive exclusivity content is heavily co-supplied by invariant co-text (per contract: consistency ≠ universally established, high frequency ≠ truth, a resistant lexicalized/nominal class caps at MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE). No occurrence carries a DIFFERENT meaning, so there is no unbridged class forcing UNRESOLVED; the honest result is one nucleus, PREFERRED, capped at MODERATE.

independent_verification: Three independent lenses (bottom-up A, distributional B, adversarial C) each returned no resistant sub-class and the same exclusivity nucleus; the plural cases (22:31, 98:5) independently corroborate the singular's meaning off the Abraham formula.
candidate_root_contribution: In the Quran the root ح-ن-ف surfaces only as the single lexicalized adjective ḥanīf (sg. حَنِيفًا) and its plural (حُنَفَاءَ), always a state-descriptor (ḥāl or kāna-predicate), never a verb, maṣdar, or other derivative. Its narrowest defensible sense is: the standing state of exclusive, non-associating devotion oriented to Allah alone — set against shirk and against confessional (Jewish/Christian) identity. This is a manner of orientation, distinct from and additional to submission (muslim), devotion (qānit), sincerity (mukhliṣ), and good-doing (muḥsin), all of which are named separately beside it.

layer_attribution.occurrence_evidence: 12/12 occurrences read; all form N, one lexeme in two inflections — sg HaniyfFA (10×: 10:105, 16:120, 16:123, 2:135, 30:30, 3:67, 3:95, 4:125, 6:161, 6:79) and pl HunafaA^'a (2×: 22:31, 98:5); all are state-descriptors (ḥāl or kāna-predicate), none an action.
layer_attribution.derivation: The root never verbalizes and produces no maṣdar, participle, or other nominal — a single frozen faʿīl adjective with sg/pl allomorphy only; morphology is therefore uninformative for meaning and permits no root-vs-lexeme triangulation.
layer_attribution.lexical_class: One lexicalized adjectival class 'ḥanīf' meaning the state of exclusive, non-associating orientation to Allah alone; a sub-collocation 'millata Ibrāhīma ḥanīfan' (5/12) is itself lexicalized and is the class that caps the grade at MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE.
layer_attribution.contextual_relation: Anti-shirk / exclusive-devotion framing accompanies all 12 (mushrik-negation ~10/12; ghayra mushrikīna bihi 22:31; mukhliṣīna 98:5; fiṭra 30:30; aslama wajhahu 4:125) and the wajh 'turning the face' imagery appears in 4/12 — but this contextual and directional material is co-text (wjh/qwm/shrk/khlṣ roots), NOT the meaning of ḥanīf itself, and must not be promoted into the root claim.
layer_attribution.reconciliation: Preliminary RESISTANT readings of 3:67 (confessional-label) and 98:5 (non-directional) were reconciled to CONSISTENT: 3:67 retains the shirk-negation and names ḥanīf as the non-confessional alternative; 98:5 carries the exclusivity core off the Abraham/wajh frames, demoting 'turning the face' to a non-defining realization. No occurrence remained finally resistant.
layer_attribution.unresolved_resistance: No semantic counterexample and no unbridged second class exist, so the result is not UNRESOLVED; the residual, un-eliminable uncertainty is that the word's distinctive positive content cannot be fully isolated from its invariant collocates and the bleached-Abrahamic-epithet competitor cannot be decisively disproven — this underdetermination is the reason STRONG/UNIVERSAL is withheld.

hard_cases.reason: Deploys ḥanīf inside a confessional taxonomy and pairs it with muslim, the point where its independent contribution is hardest to isolate and the lexicalized-identity competitor is strongest.

evidence_basis.statement: In 3:67 ḥanīf sits inside a confessional taxonomy (yahūdī / naṣrānī / ḥanīf) and is paired with muslim (ḥanīfan musliman), pulling it toward a lexicalized Abrahamic identity label; the non-redundancy of the pairing still shows it contributes distinct anti-shirk exclusivity rather than 'submitter'.

hard_cases.reason: Only singular occurrence with no explicit shirk-negation; tests whether the anti-shirk charge is intrinsic or co-text-supplied.

evidence_basis.statement: 4:125 is the only singular use with no explicit mushrikīn negation; its exclusivity is carried lexically by 'aslama wajhahu lillāh', showing the anti-shirk content can be co-supplied by neighbours rather than intrinsic to the word.

hard_cases.reason: Only occurrence whose exclusivity is routed through fiṭra rather than an adjacent shirk/ikhlāṣ term, testing 'natural conformity' vs 'anti-shirk orientation'.

evidence_basis.statement: 30:30 anchors exclusivity through fiṭra ('fiṭrata llāh ... dhālika l-dīn al-qayyim') rather than an adjacent shirk/ikhlāṣ term, testing whether the nucleus is 'natural conformity' vs 'anti-shirk orientation'; it passes under exclusive-orientation but shows the sense leans on the locally supplied positive term.

hard_cases.reason: Plural, outside both the Ibrāhīm and wajh frames, glossed by ikhlāṣ; forces the invariant to be stated as exclusivity rather than 'turning'.

evidence_basis.statement: 98:5 (plural) stands outside both the Ibrāhīm frame and the wajh frame and is glossed by adjacent ikhlāṣ ('mukhliṣīna lahu l-dīn'), stripping the directional 'turning the face' component and forcing the invariant to be stated as exclusivity toward Allah alone rather than 'turning'.

hard_case_representation.rationale: No occurrence carries a different or resistant meaning, so there is no RESISTANT_SEAM; but four occurrences function as genuine adversarial-boundary / structural-atypicality stress tests that expose the two real limits on the account — its single lexicalized form and its context-supplied positive content — and each is documented from its own verse evidence.

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: A ḥanīf/ḥunafāʾ occurrence in which the term denotes something other than exclusive non-associating orientation to Allah alone — e.g. a neutral communal/lineage identity, a ritual act, or a 'wavering/inclining' motion sense — such that the exclusivity reading is not merely co-supplied but contradicted.
rejection_condition.search_location: All 12 attestations, especially the non-Ibrāhīm and non-wajh cases (22:31, 98:5) and the confessional-taxonomy case (3:67), where the fixed anti-shirk formula is absent or the term is used as a category label.
rejection_condition.verification_method: For each occurrence remove the adjacent positive/negative anchor (lillāh, mushrik-negation, mukhliṣīn, fiṭra) and test whether ḥanīf still constrains toward exclusive orientation or collapses into a bleached honorific; check whether any use is grammatically an action/community rather than a state.
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Distinguish content intrinsic to ḥanīf from content donated by invariant co-text; do not credit the shirk-negation formula (present in ~10/12) as independent attestations of the word's own meaning; hold the lexicalized 'millata Ibrāhīma ḥanīfan' formula (5/12) as a single collocation, not five independent proofs.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If a genuine contradicting sense is found, the single-nucleus account is downgraded to UNRESOLVED/multi-class; if instead the term proves bleached in all cases, research_state drops toward REJECTED for an intrinsic-meaning claim while the deployment-level exclusivity description survives only as contextual.

reopen_conditions: If a segment-level Arabic alignment or expanded corpus reveals any ح-ن-ف verb, maṣdar, or non-faʿīl derivative, reopen to test whether a root-level nucleus (e.g. 'incline/turn') can finally be separated from the frozen adjective ḥanīf.

If any occurrence of ḥanīf/ḥunafāʾ is found used as a bare communal/lineage label OR without any adjacent exclusivity anchor (no lillāh, no mushrik-negation, no ikhlāṣ, no fiṭra, no aslama wajhahu) yet still carrying the exclusivity reading, reopen to re-test whether the anti-shirk content is intrinsic rather than co-supplied — currently unresolvable because 3:67 and 4:125 already sit at that boundary.

falsification_evidence.status_rationale: Adversarial testing (Lens C) sought a semantic counterexample across all 12 and found none: every occurrence is compatible with exclusive non-associating devotion to Allah alone, and distinctiveness holds (3:67's not-Jew/not-Christian contrast and the non-synonymy 'ḥanīfan musliman' show ḥanīf does work qānit/muslim/mukhliṣ do not). The account survives refutation, so PASSED — but strength stays MODERATE because the survival is capped by the single lexicalized form and heavy co-text scaffolding, not by any failing occurrence.
